newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Gulf Arabs worried over weevil threat to date palms.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs worried over weevil threat to date palms.

text.p: Agriculture authorities in the Arabian peninsula are researching what they fear could be a new threat to date palms -- weevil infestation.

Matthew Evans, Middle East director of Britain's National Remote Sensing Centre Ltd (NRSC) said his company has been asked to explore the feasibility of analysing the health of date palms in the Arabian peninsula with the help of satellites.
"One project the company has been asked to examine is that of the red palm weevil which we understand has the potential to devastate date palms throughout the Arabian peninsula," he told Reuters.
"We could use satellite imagery to help detect the early stages of infestation by the red palm weevil and monitor its spread," he said, adding the leaves of an infested palm turn yellow and wilt.
Evans said various agricultural and other agencies in the region were looking into ways to track the movement of the red palm weevil, or Rhynochropharus ferrugineus, which is infesting date palms.
Authorities say the red palm weevil is attacking the internal structure of date palms in some parts of the Arabian peninsula and killing them within months, Evans said.

Similar work -- using satellite remote sensing, meteorological and ground observation and entomological information -- has been carried out in sub-Saharan Africa to predict the likely movements of swarms of locusts, he added.

Dates are a popular food in the Gulf and one of the region's main crops. Saudi Arabia -- the biggest country in the peninsula and a major Gulf date producer -- has over 12 million date palms, official and other estimates show. They show that the kingdom produced 572,000 tonnes of dates last year, worth $203 million.
NSRC is 45 percent owned by Matra Marconi.
